info.description: # Beans Route API Collection API collection generated from [Beans AI tutorials](https://github.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/tree/main/beans-route) ## Overview This collection provides comprehensive API endpoints for managing logistics operations including: - **Warehouses** - Set up and manage warehouse locations - **Assignees** - Manage drivers and personnel - **Routes** - Create and manage delivery routes - **Stops** - Add and manage stops/items on routes - **Route Optimization** - Optimize stop sequences for efficiency - **Documentation** - Capture proof of delivery, signatures, and notes ## Authentication All requests use the `{{Auth}}` environment variable for authorization. Set up your Postman environment with: | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | `Auth` | Your full authorization header value (e.g., `YOUR_API_KEY`) | | `userBuid` | Your user BUID for account operations | ## Base URL ``` https://isp.beans.ai ``` ## Getting Started 1. Import this collection into Postman 2. Create/select a Postman **Environment** with `Auth` and `userBuid` variables 3. Start with **Warehouses Management** to create a warehouse 4. Create **Assignees** (drivers) 5. Create **Routes** and add **Stops** 6. Use **Route Optimization** to optimize delivery sequences

item.name: Assignees Management

request.description:
# Create Assignees

Create one or more assignees (drivers, managers, etc.) in bulk.

## Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `list_assignee_id` | string | Yes | Unique identifier for the assignee |
| `name` | string | Yes | Display name |
| `email` | string | No | Email address |
| `role` | string | Yes | One of: ADMIN, DRIVER, MANAGER, DISPATCHER |
| `disable_invite_communication` | boolean | No | Set to `true` to prevent email notifications |

## Example

```json
{
  "assignee": [
    {
      "list_assignee_id": "driver-001",
      "name": "John Smith",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "role": "DRIVER",
      "disable_invite_communication": false
    }
  ]
}
```

# Update Assignee

Update an existing assignee's properties.

## Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Updated display name |
| `code` | string | Optional assignee code |
| `state` | string | State: ACTIVE or DISABLED |
| `role` | string | Role: ADMIN, DRIVER, MANAGER, DISPATCHER |
| `employeeId` | string | Employee identifier |
| `listWarehouseId` | string | Associated warehouse ID |

## Example

```json
{
  "name": "Updated Driver Name",
  "state": "ACTIVE",
  "role": "DRIVER",
  "employeeId": "EMP-001",
  "listWarehouseId": "warehouse-123"
}
```

# Get Assignee List

Retrieve all assignees in your account.

## Response

Returns an array of assignee objects containing:
- `listAssigneeId` - Unique identifier
- `name` - Display name
- `email` - Email address
- `state` - ACTIVE or DISABLED
- `role` - Assignee role
- `latitude`/`longitude` - Last known location

# Get Assignee

Retrieve a specific assignee by their ID.

## Path Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `list-assignee-id` | The unique identifier of the assignee |

# Delete Assignee

Soft-delete an assignee. The assignee record is retained but marked as `DISABLED`.

## Important Notes

- This is a **soft-delete** operation
- The assignee will still appear in GET responses with `state: "DISABLED"`
- The assignee can no longer be assigned to routes

# Assignees Management

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

The Beans Route API provides comprehensive assignee management capabilities through five core operations. Assignees represent personnel (drivers, managers, etc.) within the system and can be created, updated, retrieved, or deleted.

## Key Operations

| Operation | Method | Endpoint |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Create | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/assignees` |
| Update | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/assignees/{id}` |
| Get List | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/assignees` |
| Get One | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/assignees/{id}` |
| Delete | DELETE | `/enterprise/v1/lists/assignees/{id}` |

## Core Fields

The Assignee Object includes:

- **Identity data**: name, email, phone
- **Operational properties**: state, role
- **Location tracking**: latitude/longitude for real-time positioning
- **Compliance features**: safety status, warehouse association
- **Code field**: Optional assignee identifier separate from primary ID

## Notable Features

### Role Taxonomy
Assignees support the following roles:
- `ADMIN`
- `DRIVER`
- `MANAGER`
- `DISPATCHER`

### Location Awareness
Real-time latitude/longitude tracking for active assignees.

### Safety Compliance
Integrated safety status monitoring with provider integration tracking.

### Hierarchical Structure
Manager associations enable organizational representation.

### Routing Eligibility
The `isAssigningEnabled` flag controls dispatch assignment capability.

## Important Notes

- **Creation**: POST requests allow bulk assignee addition with optional email notifications controlled via `disable_invite_communication`
- **Updates**: Individual assignees are modified using their list assignee ID
- **Deletion**: Implements soft-delete functionality—removed assignees retain records but transition to `DISABLED` state

# Create Delegated Account

Create a new delegated account for a partner organization.

## Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `owner.name` | string | Yes | Account owner's name |
| `owner.email` | string | Yes | Account owner's email |
| `owner.phone` | string | No | Phone number |
| `owner.password` | string | Yes | Account password |
| `name` | string | Yes | Account/organization name |
| `timezone` | string | Yes | Timezone (e.g., "America/New_York") |
| `country_iso3` | string | Yes | Country code (e.g., "USA") |
| `id` | string | Yes | Unique account identifier |

## Response

Returns account details including:
- `accountBuid` - Unique account identifier for API operations
- Email confirmation
- Subscription plan details
- Creation timestamp

# Get Delegated Account List

Retrieve all delegated accounts linked to your delegator account.

## Response

Returns an array of delegated accounts with:
- Account identifiers (`accountBuid`)
- Creation timestamps
- Subscription plans
- Configuration tags

## Using the Account BUID

Once you have the `accountBuid`, use it with the `X-Beansai-On-Behalf-Of` header to perform operations on behalf of that account:

```
X-Beansai-On-Behalf-Of: <accountBuid>
```

# Delegated Accounts

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

Beans Route enables account holders to create and manage delegated accounts for partner organizations. This facilitates cross-organizational workflows through secured API integrations.

## Key Concepts

### Delegator Role
An authenticated account authorized to create and manage other accounts.

### Delegated Account
A sub-account created by a delegator for partner use.

### On Behalf Of
Operations performed by a delegator with authorization to access delegated account data.

## Prerequisites

**Important**: Organizations must contact the Beans team to enable delegator capabilities on their primary account before using these endpoints.

## Performing Operations on Behalf of Delegated Accounts

To perform actions on behalf of a delegated account, include this HTTP header:

```
X-Beansai-On-Behalf-Of: <delegated_account's accountBUID>
```

This header authorizes the delegator to perform read/update operations targeting delegated account data.

## Response Format

API responses include:
- Account's unique identifier (`accountBuid`)
- Email and subscription tier
- Creation/update timestamps
- Metadata tags indicating delegator relationships

request.description:
# Get Route Path

Get the path geometry for a route, including distance and time for each segment between stops.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `enc` | boolean | false | Return encoded polyline format |

## Response Structure

```json
{
  "line": [
    {
      "distanceM": 2574.0,
      "timeS": 209.9,
      "encoded": "gexfFde{eV?V...",
      "referenceId": "stop-02"
    },
    {
      "distanceM": 7459.2,
      "timeS": 582.7,
      "referenceId": "stop-03"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Response Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `distanceM` | Distance in meters for this segment |
| `timeS` | Travel time in seconds |
| `encoded` | Compressed polyline (when enc=true) |
| `point` | Array of coordinates (when enc=false) |
| `referenceId` | The stop ID this segment leads to |

query.description: Returns Google encoded polyline format when true

request.description:
# Get Route Path (with refresh)

Get route path with optional force refresh to recompute paths.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `enc` | boolean | Returns Google encoded polygon format when true |
| `force_refresh` | boolean | Triggers system recomputation when material changes occur |

## When to Use force_refresh

Use `force_refresh=true` when:
- Stops have been added, removed, or reordered
- You need the most up-to-date path calculations
- The cached path may be stale

item.description:
# Get Route Paths

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

Here's an example of how to get a route's paths.

## Route Stops Visualization

![Stops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/beans-route/get-route-paths/images/stops.png)

## Table of Contents

- [Example](#example)
- [Different Sequence of Stops](#different-sequence-of-stops)
- [Notes](#notes)

---

## Example

![Sequence 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/beans-route/get-route-paths/images/sequence-1.png)

Let's say we have 9 stops for route `ecdd0458-7e63-44ad-b26d-b89fded637a2-k1` and we want to get the paths for it.

### Request

```
GET {{baseURL}}/enterprise/v1/lists/routes/path/{{list-route-id}}?enc=true
```

From the response, we can see time and distance for each segment between the stops.

So, for the sequence of the stops we set, we can see from stop 1 to stop 2:
- `distanceM` is 2574.0 (meters)
- `timeS` is 209.9 (seconds)

And from stop 2 to stop 3:
- `distanceM` is 7459.2
- `timeS` is 582.7

---

## Different Sequence of Stops

![Sequence 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/beans-route/get-route-paths/images/sequence-2.png)

Now, let's switch the sequence of first and last stop and see the difference.

So we can see the result changes, from 1st stop to 2nd stop:
- `distanceM` becomes 6976.4 (from 2574.0)
- `timeS` becomes 504.5 (from 209.9)

---

## Notes

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `enc` | boolean | Whether or not to encode the path |

### Response Fields

- **encoded** - The encoded paths of route for reducing the network bandwidth (appears in first segment of "line")
- **point** - When `enc=false`, this replaces `encoded` with an array of lat/lng coordinates
- **distanceM** - Distance in meters for the segment
- **timeS** - Time in seconds for the segment
- **referenceId** - The stop ID this segment leads to

### Encoded vs Decoded

When `enc=true`:
```json
{
  "encoded": "gexfFde{eV?V?j@@XM?yICgJ...",
  "distanceM": 2574.0,
  "timeS": 209.9
}
```

When `enc=false`:
```json
{
  "point": [
    {"latitude": 37.97604, "longitude": -121.71363},
    {"latitude": 37.97604, "longitude": -121.71375}
  ],
  "distanceM": 2574.0,
  "timeS": 209.9
}
```

# Items Documentation

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

The Items Documentation API manages contextual documentation accompanying work tasks, modeled as list items. A practical example: package delivery drivers can capture recipient signatures and package status simultaneously.

## Example Signature Image

![Signature Example](https://storage.googleapis.com/beans-images/testing/small/2022-11-22/2022-11-22_b27d61c6-21d8-4188-a0e2-f184360907d2.png)

## Key Endpoints

| Operation | Method | Endpoint |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Get Documentation | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/itemsdocumentation/{list-item-id}` |
| Search by Tracking ID | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/itemsdocumentation?tracking_id=...` |
| Create Documentation | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/itemsdocumentation` |

## Core Components

The API structures documentation around three main object types:

### 1. Item Documentation Object
- List item identifiers
- Timestamps
- Notes (array of strings)
- Images (array of image objects)
- Event codes
- Metadata tags

### 2. Event Code Object
```json
{
  "code": "101",
  "name": "received"
}
```

### 3. Image Info Object
```json
{
  "url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/...",
  "type": "signature",
  "position": {
    "latitude": 38.003654,
    "longitude": -121.783137
  }
}
```

## Notable Characteristics

The documentation system permits:
- **Multiple images** and **multiple notes** per documentation record
- **Tags** for domain-specific attributes (example: package dimensions)
- **Flexible image classifications**: `proof`, `signature`, `exception`
- **Geographic coordinates** associated with captured images

# Optimize Route with Stops

Optimize a route by providing an array of stops to be reordered.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `startMode` | Yes | Where the route starts |
| `endMode` | Yes | Where the route ends |

## Start/End Mode Options

- `WAREHOUSE` - Warehouse location
- `ASSIGNEE_LOCATION` - Driver's current GPS
- `ASSIGNEE_ADDRESS` - Driver's home address
- `PREVIOUS_STOP` - Previous stop location
- `NONE` - No fixed point
- `lat,lng` - Custom coordinates

## Response

Returns optimized stops with updated `routePriority` values indicating the optimal visiting sequence.

# Optimize Entire Route

Optimize all stops on a route by route ID. No request body required.

## Important

This is a POST request **without a body**. The route ID in the URL specifies which route to optimize.

## When to Use

Use this endpoint when:
- You want to optimize all stops on an existing route
- Stops are being added dynamically
- You don't need to specify which stops to include

item.description: # Route Optimization ## Overview This section covers route optimization capabilities for reordering stops to minimize travel time and distance. ## Route Stops Example ## Key Features ### Route Optimization with Stops The API allows optimization of routes containing multiple stops by specifying start and end modes. **Important Note**: `route_priority` may not start from 1. The system uses values like 3, 6, 10, 15 to represent suggested visiting sequences. ## Start/End Mode Parameters | Mode | Description | | --- | --- | | `WAREHOUSE` | Start/end at warehouse location | | `ASSIGNEE_LOCATION` | Start/end at assignee's current GPS location | | `ASSIGNEE_ADDRESS` | Start/end at assignee's home address | | `PREVIOUS_STOP` | Start from previous stop | | `NONE` | No specific start/end point | | `lat,lng` | Custom coordinates (e.g., `37.12423,-123.2323`) | ## Request Examples ### Optimize with Stops Array ``` POST /enterprise/v1/lists/items/do/optimize/?startMode=WAREHOUSE&endMode=WAREHOUSE ``` ### Optimize Entire Route ``` POST /lists/routes/{listRouteID}/do/optimize?startMode=WAREHOUSE&endMode=WAREHOUSE ``` ## Response Structure Responses include: - Arrays of items with `listItemId`, `address`, `status`, `coordinates` - Calculated `routePriority` values indicating optimal sequence - Route objects with warehouse information and start/end modes - Path metadata including MD5 hashes for change detection

item.name: Route Optimization with Units

request.description:
# Optimize Items with Units

Group and optimize stops that share the same address.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `mode` | Yes | Grouping strategy |

## Grouping Modes

| Mode | Groups By |
|------|----------|
| `INPUT_ADDRESS` | Same input address |
| `INPUT_ADDRESS_UNIT_AND_CUSTOMER_NAME` | Address + unit + customer name |
| `INPUT_ADDRESS_AND_UNIT` | Address + unit |
| `BUILDING_ADDRESS` | Formatted address |
| `FORMATTED_ADDRESS_AND_UNIT_NO_TIME_WINDOW` | Formatted address + unit (ignores time windows) |

## Response

Grouped stops appear with a parent item containing a `children` array:

```json
{
  "listItemId": "auto-generated-id",
  "notes": "Autogenerated by optimizer",
  "numPackages": 4,
  "children": [
    {"listItemId": "original-1"},
    {"listItemId": "original-2"}
  ]
}
```

# Optimize Route with Units

Optimize an entire route with unit grouping. Useful when stops are being added dynamically.

## Important

- POST request **without a body**
- Groups all stops on the route by the specified mode
- Creates parent/child relationships for same-address stops

# Get Route Items

Get all items/stops for a specific route. Use this to see current stops before running optimization.

item.description:
# Route Optimization With Units (Grouping)

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

Route Optimization With Units is a grouping mechanism to condense stops that share the same address into parent/child relationships.

For other route optimization conditions like pickup-dropoff pair, time window, assignee shift time, capacity, please see [Dynamic Route Optimization](https://github.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/tree/main/dynamic-routes-optimization).

## Table of Contents

- [To Group stops that have same address](#to-group-stops-that-have-same-address)
- [Group by Route](#group-by-route)
- [Supported Modes](#supported-modes)

---

## To Group Stops That Have Same Address

Let's say we have 5 stops for route `a3cc1ed1-8586-426e-b154-e46bc7bf0c66`, and 4 of them are with the same address.

**Address: `9404` Central Ave, Montclair, CA 91763**
- a3cc1ed-1
- a3cc1ed-3
- a3cc1ed-4
- a3cc1ed-5

**Address: `9000` Central Ave, Montclair, CA 91763**
- a3cc1ed-2

### Grouping Request

```
POST {{baseURL}}/enterprise/v1/lists/items/do/optimizewithunits?mode=INPUT_ADDRESS
```

### Result

The stops with the same address are grouped together with a new `listItemId` under the field `children`:

```json
{
  "listItemId": "e20c85d1b155327a973e5fa41f0bd08d",
  "address": "9404 Central Ave, Montclair, CA",
  "notes": "Autogenerated by optimizer",
  "numPackages": 4,
  "children": [
    {"listItemId": "a3cc1ed-1", ...},
    {"listItemId": "a3cc1ed-3", ...},
    {"listItemId": "a3cc1ed-4", ...},
    {"listItemId": "a3cc1ed-5", ...}
  ]
}
```

---

## Group by Route

For scenarios where you want to optimize an entire route regardless of how many stops there are, use:

```
POST {{baseURL}}/lists/routes/{listRouteID}/do/optimizewithunits?mode=INPUT_ADDRESS
```

**Note**: POST request without a body.

---

## Supported Modes

| Mode | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `INPUT_ADDRESS` | Group stops with the same input address |
| `INPUT_ADDRESS_UNIT_AND_CUSTOMER_NAME` | Group by (address, unit, customer name) |
| `INPUT_ADDRESS_AND_UNIT` | Group by (address, unit) |
| `BUILDING_ADDRESS` | Group by formatted_address |
| `FORMATTED_ADDRESS_AND_UNIT_NO_TIME_WINDOW` | Group by (formatted_address, unit), ignoring time windows |

item.description:
# Routes Management

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

The Beans Route API enables comprehensive route management through CRUD operations. Routes represent delivery runs that contain stops and are assigned to drivers and warehouses.

## Core Operations

| Operation | Method | Endpoint |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Create | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/routes` |
| Update | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/routes/{id}` |
| Get List | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/routes` |
| Get One | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/routes/{id}` |
| Delete | DELETE | `/enterprise/v1/lists/routes/{id}` |

## Key Route Properties

Routes contain:
- **Identifiers**: `listRouteId`, `accountBuid`
- **Operational details**: `name`, `dateStr`, `status`
- **Relationships**: `assignee`, `warehouse` objects
- **Timestamps**: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`
- **Metadata**: `routePathMd5` for route computation tracking

## Route Status Values

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `OPEN` | Active route |
| `CLOSED` | Completed or deleted route |

## Route Types

- `DEFAULT` - Standard delivery route
- `HOLDING` - Holding area
- `SORTING_RECEIVED` - Sorting received items
- `TRAILER` - Trailer route
- `RETURN_TO_SENDER` - Return shipments

## Configuration Features

Routes support:
- Start/end mode configuration (`WAREHOUSE`, `ASSIGNEE_ADDRESS`, `STOP`)
- Secondary assignees
- Provider associations
- Tag-based preferences (e.g., timezone)

item.name: Stops Management

request.description:
# Create Stops

Create one or more stops on a route.

## Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `list_item_id` | string | Yes | Unique stop identifier |
| `address` | string | Yes | Delivery address |
| `route.list_route_id` | string | Yes | Route to add stop to |
| `type` | string | Yes | PICKUP or DROPOFF |
| `deliver_from_str` | string | No | Earliest time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) |
| `deliver_by_str` | string | No | Latest time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) |
| `placement` | string | No | Where to place: FIRST, LAST, or OPTIMAL |

## Example

```json
{
  "item": [
    {
      "list_item_id": "stop-001",
      "address": "123 Main St, Los Angeles, CA 90001",
      "route": {"list_route_id": "route-001"},
      "type": "DROPOFF",
      "deliver_from_str": "2024-01-15 09:00",
      "deliver_by_str": "2024-01-15 17:00"
    }
  ]
}
```

# Update Stop

Update an existing stop.

## ⚠️ Important: Whole Object Replacement

This performs a **whole object replacement**. You must include ALL existing values you want to maintain. Any fields not included will be cleared.

## Example

If updating just the address, you still need to include all other fields:

```json
{
  "list_item_id": "stop-001",
  "address": "New Address Here",
  "route": {"list_route_id": "route-001"},
  "type": "DROPOFF",
  "deliver_from_str": "2024-01-15 09:00",
  "deliver_by_str": "2024-01-15 17:00",
  "status": "NEW"
}
```

# Get Stop List

Retrieve all stops in your account.

# Get Stops by Route ID

Retrieve all non-deleted stops for a specific route.

# Get Stop

Retrieve a specific stop by ID.

# Get Stop by Tracking ID

Find a stop using its tracking ID.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `tracking_id` | The package tracking ID |

# Delete Stop

Soft-delete a stop. The stop is marked as `DELETED` while maintaining historical records.

# Stops Management

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

The Stops Management API enables comprehensive operations for managing delivery and pickup stops within routes. The system supports creating, updating, retrieving, and deleting stops with detailed tracking and documentation capabilities.

## Example Proof Image

![Proof Image](https://storage.googleapis.com/beans-images/testing/original/2022-03-02/2022-03-02_b695d615-4d32-4222-ba34-f34a68f1cee4.png)

## Key Operations

| Operation | Method | Endpoint |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Create | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/items` |
| Update | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/items/{id}` |
| Get List | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/items` |
| Get by Route | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/routes/{id}/items` |
| Get One | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/items/{id}` |
| Get by Tracking | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/item_by_tracking_id` |
| Delete | DELETE | `/enterprise/v1/lists/items/{id}` |

## Stop Properties

A list item (stop) encompasses:

### Core Fields
- `listItemId` - Unique identifier
- `address` - Delivery address
- `position` / `displayPosition` - Coordinates
- `status` - Current status

### Temporal Fields
- `deliverFromStr` - Earliest delivery time
- `deliverByStr` - Latest delivery time
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `statusUpdatedAt` - Timestamps

### Operational Fields
- `route` - Associated route
- `routePriority` - Sequence position
- `type` - PICKUP or DROPOFF
- `placement` - Placement notation

### Constraints
- `dimensions` - Weight, volume, count
- `flavors` - Special handling requirements
- `stopTimeSeconds` - Expected stop duration

### Documentation
- `notes` - Delivery notes
- `trackingId` - Package tracking ID
- `numPackages` - Number of packages

## Important: Update Behavior

**Update performs whole object replacement** - existing values must be included to maintain them. Any fields not included in the update request will be cleared.

# Create Warehouses

Create one or more warehouses.

## Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `list_warehouse_id` | string | Yes | Unique warehouse identifier |
| `name` | string | Yes | Display name |
| `address` | string | Yes | Physical address |
| `domicile` | string | No | Domicile identifier |

## Example

```json
{
  "warehouse": [
    {
      "list_warehouse_id": "warehouse-001",
      "name": "Main Distribution Center",
      "address": "123 Warehouse Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90001"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Response

Returns the created warehouse with:
- Geocoded `position` (latitude/longitude)
- `formattedAddress`
- `createdAt` timestamp

# Update Warehouse

Update an existing warehouse's properties.

# Get Warehouse List

Retrieve all warehouses in your account.

# Get Warehouse

Retrieve a specific warehouse by ID.

# Get Warehouse Routes

Retrieve all routes associated with a warehouse.

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `dateStr` | No | Filter by date (YYYY-MM-DD) |

## Response

Returns routes connected to this warehouse, optionally filtered by date.

# Delete Warehouse

Soft-delete a warehouse.

## Important

- This is a **soft-delete** operation
- The deleted warehouse will still appear in Get Warehouse by ID responses
- Historical data is preserved for audit purposes

# Warehouses Management

![Beans Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/beansai/beans-tutorials/main/assets/images/beans-128x128.png)

## Overview

The Beans Route API provides comprehensive warehouse management functionality, enabling users to create, update, retrieve, and delete warehouse records within their enterprise account.

Warehouses serve as start/end points for routes and are essential for route optimization.

## Core Operations

| Operation | Method | Endpoint |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Create | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/warehouses` |
| Update | POST | `/enterprise/v1/lists/warehouses/{id}` |
| Get List | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/warehouses` |
| Get One | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/warehouses/{id}` |
| Get Routes | GET | `/enterprise/v1/lists/warehouses/{id}/routes` |
| Delete | DELETE | `/enterprise/v1/lists/warehouse/{id}` |

## Warehouse Properties

Warehouse objects contain:
- **Identifiers**: `listWarehouseId`, `accountBuid`
- **Location data**: `address`, `formattedAddress`, `position` (lat/lng)
- **Timestamps**: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`
- **Display**: `name`

## Key Features

- **Automatic geocoding**: Addresses are automatically geocoded to coordinates
- **Timestamp tracking**: Full audit trail through timestamps
- **Soft-delete**: Preserves data integrity when deleting
- **Route association**: Query routes by warehouse with date filtering
- **Enterprise organization**: Warehouses are scoped to your account
